    Bundled kinetics families

    Each module owns one swappable family: its reaction definitions, symbolic DAETools hooks, component requirements, and local regularization constants. Run manifests record selected definitions, their parameter values, and the built-in definition fingerprint. They also record the source Git commit when available; packaged installations may have no Git checkout. There is no separate kinetics version system. See run provenance.

    These references document provenance. They do not assert that a family is appropriate for a particular material or experiment.

    Copper — San Pio et al.

    Source: M. A. San Pio et al., Chemical Engineering Science 175 (2018), 56–71, doi:10.1016/j.ces.2017.09.044 (online).

    • copper_sio2_san_pio (copper_sio2.py) contains the two pseudo-homogeneous CuO → Cu2O → Cu hydrogen-reduction steps and the Cu + ½O2 → CuO oxidation step. SiO2 is treated as an inert support, so the family requires no aluminium or spinel species.
    • copper_al2o3_san_pio (copper_al2o3.py) contains those support-independent reductions, Cu → CuO oxidation, and the Al2O3-specific spinel reduction and oxidation steps.

    Both families use the Cu oxidation rate law r = k(T) c_Cu sqrt(p_O2) with oxygen partial pressure in bar, but the paper fits different Arrhenius parameters: Table 5 gives A = 0.193 s^-1 bar^-1/2 and Ea = 180 J/mol for SiO2, while Table 9 gives A = 0.854 s^-1 bar^-1/2 and Ea = 830 J/mol for Al2O3. The SiO2 oxidation hook copies the Al2O3 rate expression and smooth positive-pressure regularization, using the SiO2-specific parameter defaults.

    The source states that CuO-to-Cu reduction is independent of the support and extends that base model with CuAl2O4/CuAlO2 chemistry for the Al2O3 carrier. The zero-order hydrogen reductions retain a local smooth gas-availability gate.

    Both copper families evaluate the smooth positive pressure (p + sqrt(p*p + 4*epsilon*epsilon))/2, with epsilon = 1e-12 bar, using an algebraically equivalent rationalized form in regularization.py. This preserves the small positive tail and its derivative for negative trial pressures without subtracting nearly equal numbers. The rate laws and regularization scale are unchanged.

    Nickel redox — Medrano form

    nickel_medrano (nickel_medrano.py) follows the Medrano-style form documented in Andrew Wright, Chemical Looping Reactor Modelling – 2D, with context from doi:10.1016/j.apenergy.2015.08.078 (online). The rational, solver-oriented implementation is canonical; the older duplicate form is not retained.

    The chemical rate constant includes the total-pressure correction used by Argyris et al., Sustainable Energy & Fuels 6 (2022), 2755–2770, doi:10.1039/D2SE00351A (online), Eq. (14) and Table 2:

    kj(T,P)=k0,jexp(−Ea,jRT)(PPref)−qj,Pref=1 bar=105 Pa.

    P is the local absolute total gas pressure, recovered from C_total R T. The reference pressure is fixed at 1 bar. This factor modifies the chemical rate constant inside the shrinking-core resistance expression; the ash diffusivity is unchanged. Gas concentration retains its existing reaction-order dependence. At 1 bar the additional factor is exactly one. Each reaction exposes its own dimensionless, nonnegative exponent.

    Nickel-catalysed reforming

    • reforming_xu_froment (reforming_xu_froment.py) implements the three Xu–Froment reactions from doi:10.1002/aic.690350109 (online).
    • reforming_numaguchi (reforming_numaguchi.py) implements the alternative Numaguchi–Kikuchi reforming and water-gas-shift form documented in Andrew Wright's technical report.

    These are alternative published mechanisms, not compatibility aliases.

    Iron redox — He et al.

    iron_he (iron_he.py) contains the He et al. reduction and oxidation family from Energy Conversion and Management 293 (2023), 117525. Its symbolic runtime expressions and local constants are the canonical implementation.
